messages:
marco: Hey team — customer ACME reports intermittent 502/504s from Hosted API around 11:18-11:24 UTC during a large batch embeddings job. They see errors only when payloads exceed ~5MB. They provided an example request id: req_0a7b2c3d and a short curl repro below. Can someone triage?

customer-acme: We started a bulk embed run (~20k texts, chunked) and at ~50% progress hit repeated 504s, then a flood of client retries. No change on our side. Logs show connection reset from upstream.

anya: Got it — assigning eng-sre. First guess: ingress downstream connpool/stream saturation or upstream auth proxy backpressure. marco, can you paste the raw response headers/traces and the curl you used?

marco: Pasting minimal repro and returned headers/log snippet: 

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDDIT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","inputs":["...(big payload)..."]}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```

Response snippet: 
```
HTTP/2 504 \ndate: Tue, 25 May 2026 11:19:42 GMT
content-type: application/json
server: envoy
X-Request-Id: req_0a7b2c3d
via: 1.1 redwood-edge
```

Upstream log: `upstream reset before response: RST_STREAM 2`

anya: Thanks. Can you also include `x-envoy-upstream-service-time` if present? That'll show if upstream processing hit a hard timeout.

marco: Not in this snippet. I asked customer for more traces; they sent a short tcpdump showing a flurry of `RST` after ~30s for some streams.

pagerbot: [alert] hostedapi-edge-high-4xx-5xx spike — cluster=ingress-prod region=us-west-2 rate=220/min (threshold 100). Paging eng-sre on-call.

derek: Jumping in. Two quick things to check: 1) ingress h2 concurrency/stream limits per connection (we've bumped defaults in canary recently), 2) upstream gateway auth cache/backpressure — a sudden large number of long-lived streams can exhaust keepalive slots causing Envoy to RST.

kate: Customer mentioned chunking payloads. If they switched from per-item requests to big batched payloads, that would keep streams open longer and increase KV cache pressure for auth or embeddings model nodes.

anya: Repro plan: 1) replicate with a synthetic job from our perf runner with similar batch sizes and chunking to validate before rolling config, 2) temporarily gate customer at edge with rate-limit/burst cap to stop retries, 3) collect full `envoy` and `ingress` logs around req_0a7b2c3d.

marco: I'll ask customer to pause and give us a window. Meanwhile, I ran a quick internal test: reproduced 504s after ~8 concurrent large streams. Attached short logs: 
```
[ingress] 11:18:39 conn 0x7f -> stream 12 created
[ingress] 11:18:40 stream 12 wait for upstream slot
[ingress] 11:18:42 upstream connect failed: no available connection
[ingress] 11:18:42 reset stream 12 RST_STREAM
```

derek: That pattern looks like connection pool exhaustion on the upstream (auth or model router). Two mitigations: increase max connections per host temporarily, or enable a short circuit policy to fail fast on long payloads. Both need risk review. For immediate stopgap: ask support to apply a transient per-tenant concurrency cap via rate-limiter to reduce simultaneous long streams.

anya: agree. Also check for recent Envoy config flip — did we change `http2_max_concurrent_streams` or pool sizing in last deploy? eng-releases might have a note.

marco: Customer paused. I'll implement a temporary limiter on their tenant (cap concurrent requests to 6) and see if errors stop.

kate: On long-term: if model backpressure is causing upstream RSTs we should add sentinel metrics: per-tenant long-stream gauge, auth cache eviction rate, and keepalive slot usage. That will help detect before customer hit.

derek: For repro I can run a stress job against a staging ingress with identical h2 settings. If we reproduce, we can test two fixes: 1) bump upstream pool by 25% and 2) switch to short-lived per-request auth tokens to reduce cache pins.

marco: Update — after capping concurrency at 6, customer reports no new 5xxs and completed remaining job with slower throughput. They will gradually increase to test thresholds.

anya: Great. Next steps: derek to run staging repro and propose safe config change, platform to add sentinel metrics, support to keep customer on slower cadence until final fix. Assign owners: derek=eng-runtime, kate=product/obs, marco=support, anya=eng-sre.

customer-acme: Thanks for quick triage. We'll keep you posted if we see regressions when we ramp back up.

marco: Closing loop — I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem if derek reproduces and we require a deploy. For now marking as mitigated. :white_check_mark:
